why: Going down each column, the figure turns 90 degrees clockwise. In the third column the black point goes from the top edge to the right edge, so next it turns to the bottom-left, like the very first figure. Option 1 fits. Option 3 has the black point at the top, which is the first figure of that column again.
trick: In grids of turning shapes, check rows and columns; here the columns hold the rule.
note: The book key says option 1; the column-rotation rule agrees.
